tips.comment: James Fanshawe likes to bring his horses on slowly giving them time to learn. First run in a handicap today and Oisin Murphy in the plate, must have a great chance in this low level affair.

19 days ago saw the Marco Botti-trained 3yo return from a 181-day break on handicap debut. Ridden by Hollie Doyle (again today), she had obviously trained on, finishing 4th of 12, beaten just over a length. She was strong at the finish and should be more of a finished article today and can break her maiden tag.
I'm hoping George Bass's 3lb claim will get Alcazan in the mix here at Lingfield. I put this pick out on my Twitter at 20/1, and it has already been backed in to 12's.

Crafter can go well for the Loughnane yard. Crafter has won over track and trip before and ran a very good run at this Lingfield track as well last time out when finishing in second. Crafter is only 1 pound higher in the ratings today and can do better.
Saturnalia drops a pound plus gets another 3lb from the jockey riding in Taylor Fisher, and that could just do the trick. If not, it looks like the each-way shot today.

Mister Mojito is friendless in the early market but looks the e/w value in the race to me. He won easily on his only previous run at the course over a furlong less and a repeat of that would be good enough to see him go close here. He disappointed at Kempton last time out when slowly away and pulling too hard but that was a seasonal debut run, and he should do better here with the first time tongue tie possibly providing extra improvement. The trainer is in great form too so I'll back this one e/w despite the unease in the market.

Blue Collar Lad has found himself an excellent opportunity to bounce back to form here after a below par effort at Kempton he has had 40 days off to get over that and he arrives here operating on a very dangerous mark of 50 with the cheeckpieces re applied this looks to be a very thin class 6 handicap where Blue Collar Lad can make his presence strongly felt of his easing mark jockey Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride and can give Blue Collar Lad the perfect ride here at Lingfield price at the time of writing represents strong E/W value given the nature of this race must be taken seriously and accordingly

Galel looks poised for a big run here with this race representing a drop in class to a very thin looking class 6 handicap and a step back up in trip both those factors being good moves by his connections currently operating on a mark of 55 this daughter of Exceed And Excel & Gallipot ( Dam's sire Galileo ) is likely to be much better than a mark of 55 and is likely to have a big performance in the locker just waiting to be unleashed in very good time jockey David Egan takes the ride that being another positive and he can greatly assist Galel in showcasing a much better piece of form this time out needs considering in a race of this nature
Brinton won a few starts ago at Southwell over 1m. The form looks okay, and he has been consistent of late. Probably doesn't need to improve much to figure. Well drawn.

A very poor-looking handicap where Cherry Hill appeals. He has been running creditably off higher marks than today's, and this step up in trip looks like a move in the right direction. He has had a little break, so will be nice and fresh.

Briefly gets weight from her two rivals here despite the handicapper deciding to put her up six pounds after finishing a half-length 2nd of 9 to Badbury Rings over course and distance last month, running after a six-month break. It is her two rivals who arrive from a break this time.

Mr Mackay has not run over this far before but likes the better going. He won over two miles three and a half furlongs on good at Huntingdon back in 2023. In this four-horse race, the pace is not likely to be strong, and Toby McCain-Mitchell is a good jockey for his three-pound claim.

Recently changed trainer to Paul Nicholls. Placed second in a race in France after a longer distance. Making its first appearance with a Hood, hopefully, should make a difference and get him off to a strong career.

Space Voyage has to carry a seven-pound penalty for her easy win at Market Rasen last week. She was held up until the final bend but took it up three out and then eased away from the field. She could be rated even higher. Beau M Morgan takes off his five-pound allowance to take her weight down to twelve stone four pounds, but she still has to give weight to the field.
David Noonan is back on board. Back to ideal trip and dropped in weight and grade. Poor race so should go close.

Jaramillo sets the standard here with a very good 3rd last time out at Southwell, Theformismighty won that race, but Jaramillo finished in front of Awaythelad and Yes Day who won today (23rd). Dropped 4lbs since his last run. James Bowen rides again. He should go well. Every chance.
Likely to be a cut above these, winning two 1-mile maidens before improving again. Stepped up to this sort of trip to win nicely on handicap debut LTO. Surely more to come here from 4 lbs higher.
A strong horse with a lot of experience under its saddle. Shouldn't have too many issues with the extra weight on board. Has recently dropped in official rating but shouldn't matter too much.

Course and distance winner who was last seen at Southwell 20 days ago where finishing 9th/12 however this gelded son of Zoustar is no horse to overlook and he is the type to bounce back quickly especially having found a suitable looking race to get involved in here currently operating on a mark of 66 which is well within his capabilities expect to see Zu Run thundering home in the closing argument of this class 5 handicap with jockey Billy Loughnane taking ride that most certainly being a positive merits consideration

Thapa VC gets a kindly drop in grade and hasn't been running that bad under Jack Mitchell. But it gets a good jockey change here in Rossa Ryan, which can only help its cause as it continues to fall in weight. Good each way.

I like the look of Twilight Romance at this price. He has been competing in better races than this, and his last race, also at Wolverhampton, looked like a strong race to me. This is his third outing after a long break and wind surgery, and I think he will be ready to roll.

Billy Loughnane usually gets a big-priced one in, so why not try one not seen for a while or had just the one AW run... Jungle Land! Now, the stable took this race last year. Will lightning strike twice?

Well drawn, front running sprinter going for a yard in form. Back up to 6 furlongs after a couple of races at 5. Last 2 goes at 6, both placed efforts, were also in Class 3 races. The drop to class 4 should be appreciated and should be competitive.

Gunfighter is the rank outsider here but is 2 from 3 on Tapeta and is only 3lb higher than his last win, which was an easy one on his last visit to this course. He makes his 4-year-old debut here, and the first-time booking of David Probert is a good one for the horse's new stable since he rides this course well. Gunfighter also should have the early pace to make the most of being drawn in stall 4, and 14/1 looks decent value.
Has been in good form and can follow up his two Newcastle wins and achieve a hat-trick here off only a 3 lbs higher mark.
Heartrate had a nice win by a neck last time out over course and distance. Gone up to a mark of 52, can win again!
Raul de Silva gave Shamardia an excellent run LTO when finishing second behind Stella Hogan, who went on to place third in a tough Class 5 race. I think we will see him being in the mix again.

I still think there could be yet another win in Red Walls, especially now ridden by Eddie Greatrex, who was the last to win on it. Hovers around that mark, and its well-being still looks positive after a blast out and getting caught close home. Maybe overpriced here.
C&D winner on her only other start from a pound higher last July. She made all of the running that day and has been drawn in one here so is perfectly drawn to attack early again.
